CIII. Ne pereant et euanescant ab labili hominum memoria gesta et cause rerum propter aimorum dierumve prolixitatem, discretorum virorum ea solet sollercia per litteras eternare. Hinc est, quod nos frater Albertus dictus abbas in Altovado tam presentibus quam futu- ris per has paginas volumus esse notum, quod noster olim fundator graciosus dominus Petrus de Rosenberch memorie deuote inter ce tera pietatis caritatisque opera multa atque multa bona, que nostro monasterio sueque et progenitorum suorum fundacioni impendit et ostendit, nostro conuentui et camere specialiter donauit ac dedit ob sui dilecti awnculi remedium Johannis de Dobruschka sexagenas gros- sorum centum promptorum monete Pragensis bac videlicet sub condi cione, vt de quinquaginta sexagenis denariorum perhermiter annis singulis specialiter nostro in conuentu agatur suus anniuersarius dies cum missis et orationibus specialibus secundum nostri ordinis 110 conmendabilem consuetudinem, et ipso die ex prouidencia domini abbatis, qui pro tempore fuerit, in refectorio fratribus de prandio melius et humanius debet atque benignius prouideri. De reliquis quinquaginta sexagenis a nostre domus camerario quicunque fuerit toti conuentui omnibus et singulis annis eternaliter debent ministran tunice noue vnicuique fratri turneam nouam, prout melius vestiarius poterit comparare; nam prius nimiam ipsius monasterii ob penuriam et paupertatem fratribus vltra duos anuos de camera tunice noue da- bantur. Hanc autem supradicte summe pecuniam videlicet quinqua ginta sexagenas noster bone recordaeionis suscepit antecessor dominus Thomas huius loci abbas et in vsus necessarios monasterii nostri impendit et consumpsit atque conuentui pro pecunia eadeni, ne conuentus aliquo modo temporibus futuris sui vestibus solacio per aliquem suorum successorum priuaretur, pro conuentu deputauit domo camere, quam diu predicta pecunia insoluta permaneret, cer- tam atque decimam in Predall bonam omnibus annis a camerario tol- lendam atque recipiendam, donec ipsi conuentui de ¡am locuta pecunia videlicet quinquaginta sexagenis satisfieret. De quibus tamen dena- riis personaliter, dum adhuc viueret, in viginti libris denariorum sa tisfecit atque soluit. Nos vero per cetera summa non soluta ad in- stanciam multam ac magnam atque communem nostri conuentus vo- luntatem specialiter cum ex omnium seniorum nostrorum consensu damns et imperpetuum perpetuamus nostre domus camere certos annuos redditus in nostris bonis in Luppollsching quinque talenla denariorum Pataviensis Wyennensisve monete et quinquaginta dena- rios, quos ipse vestiarius, qui protunc fuerit, recipere et colligere debet per singulos annos in festo beati Georii medios et in festo sancti Mychahelis medios, et exinde toti conuentui prouidere de suo vestitu, sicuti est superius diffinitum. In cuius rei testimonium sigil- lari iussimus presentes paginas nostro et nostri conuentus sigillo necnon reuerendi domini domini Wernhardi patris abbatis ac visita- toris nostri de Hylaria et nostrorum gratiosorum et generosorum fundatorum sigillis domini Petri ac domini Judoci fratris sui de Ro- senberch. entries.english:
1354, 4 January. Albert, Abt von Hohenfurt, again assigns revenues from his estates at Luppetschnig to secure a sum owed to his convent.

CIII. Lest deeds and the causes of events perish and vanish from the fleeting memory of men through the passage of many years or days, prudent men customarily preserve them in writing. Therefore I, Brother Albert, called abbot at Altovado, wish it to be known through these pages to all present and future that our former gracious founder, Lord Peter von Rosenberg, mindful of the many good works of piety and charity that he bestowed upon and demonstrated for our monastery, its foundation, and that of his ancestors, gave and donated to our convent and especially its chamber one hundred sexagenae of ready Prague groschen for the salvation of the soul of his beloved uncle Johann de Dobruschka, on this condition: of fifty sexagenae, his anniversary shall be celebrated every year in perpetuity in our convent, especially with Masses and special prayers according to the praiseworthy custom of our order; and on that day, at the provision of the abbot then in office, the brothers are to be provided with a better, more humane, and more generous meal in the refectory. From the remaining fifty sexagenae, whoever is chamberlain of our house shall every year forever provide new tunics to the whole convent, a new tunic for each brother, of the best kind the keeper of the wardrobe can procure. For previously, because the monastery was exceedingly poor and in want, the brothers received new tunics from the chamber only once every two years.

Our predecessor of good memory, Lord Thomas, abbot of this place, received the aforesaid sum of money, namely fifty sexagenae, and spent it on the necessary uses of our monastery. So that the convent might not in future be deprived by any of his successors of the benefit of clothing on account of this money, he assigned for the convent, from the chamber estate and for as long as the money remained unpaid, a certain annual income and tithe from an estate at Predall, to be collected and received by the chamberlain every year until the convent had been repaid the aforesaid fifty sexagenae. Of this money, while still alive, he personally paid and settled twenty pounds of denarii.

As the rest of the sum remains unpaid, at the repeated and earnest request and common will of our convent, and especially with the consent of all our elders, we grant and perpetually assign to the chamber of our house certain annual revenues from our estates at Luppetschnig: five talents of Passau or Viennese currency and fifty denarii. The keeper of the wardrobe then in office is to receive and collect these each year, half at the feast of Saint George and half at the feast of Saint Michael, and use them to provide clothing for the whole convent as specified above. In witness of this matter, we have ordered these pages to be sealed with our seal and that of our convent, as well as with the seals of the reverend Lord Wernhard, our father abbot and visitor from Wilhering, and of our gracious and noble founders, Lord Peter and his brother Lord Jodok de Rosenberch. Given in the year of the Lord 1354, on the octave of the Holy Innocents.

Five seals hang from parchment strips. (a) Not very large, etc.; see CII, a. The seal of Abbot Albert of Altovado; it is impressed in green wax. (b) See the seal of the Hohenfurt convent at CXL. (c) Above it, the seal of the abbot of Wilhering, here in red wax; see CII, c. (d) The small seal of Peter von Rosenberg is described in the following document. (e) Likewise the seal of Jodok. The latter three seals are in red wax, while the second is impressed in white wax.
